slot.brief: Which amine (primary/secondary/tertiary) gives a foul smell with chloroform and KOH, and identify the product formed.

stem: Methylamine is heated with chloroform and alcoholic KOH. Which pair correctly gives the amine class that reacts and the foul-smelling product formed?

verdicts.working: Methylamine is a primary amine. Primary amines react with chloroform and alcoholic KOH to form foul-smelling isocyanides; here the product is methyl isocyanide.

working:
$\text{CH}_3\text{NH}_2+\text{CHCl}_3+3\text{KOH}\rightarrow\text{CH}_3\text{NC}+3\text{KCl}+3\text{H}_2\text{O}$. The carbylamine reaction is given by primary amines; $\text{CH}_3\text{NC}$ is methyl isocyanide.

Independent check: Methylamine is a primary amine. Primary amines react with chloroform and alcoholic KOH to form foul-smelling isocyanides; here the product is methyl isocyanide.
solution:
The carbylamine reaction is given by primary amines with chloroform and alcoholic KOH.
$$\text{CH}_3\text{NH}_2+\text{CHCl}_3+3\text{KOH}\rightarrow\text{CH}_3\text{NC}+3\text{KCl}+3\text{H}_2\text{O}$$
Thus, methylamine forms the foul-smelling product methyl isocyanide.
